text: F-strings do far more than drop a variable into some text.
We start with a float and a short string to play with.
Put an f before the quote, and anything in curly braces gets evaluated.
Colon dot two f is a format spec — round this float to two decimal places.
So pi prints as three point one four, not the full messy value.
Format specs handle padding and thousands separators too, all inside the braces.
Bang r calls repr instead of str, which keeps the quotes visible around the string.
And you can run real expressions inside the braces, like len of name.
The equals sign suffix is the debugging trick — it prints the expression and its value.
x equals five, written once, shown as both the name and the result.
That saves you writing the variable name twice every time you debug.
